add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.texto: readLength() validates `length >= limit` where `limit` is the total input array size, not the remaining bytes. This lets malformed lengths that are larger than the remaining stream but smaller than the total array pass validation, so parsing fails only later with EOF instead of being rejected early. Compare against the actual remaining bytes (e.g., `is.available()`) or track remaining bytes explicitly.

readLength() returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding, but readSequence() interprets `-1` as zero content and returns an empty list, while readInteger() would call `read(-1)` and throw NegativeArraySizeException. Reject indefinite-length encoding with an IOException in readLength(), or handle the sentinel explicitly in both callers.

readLength validates length against the total array size (`limit`) instead of the bytes remaining in the stream. A malformed length that exceeds the remaining bytes but is smaller than the total input passes the check, so readSequence can over-consume trailing bytes and the caller gets a generic EOF/IO error instead of an early out-of-bounds rejection. Track remaining bytes (`limit - count`) and reject `length > remaining`.

readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, and readSequence treats -1 as zero content and returns an empty list. Since this decoder is intended for DER (definite-length) ECDSA signatures, indefinite-length input should be rejected explicitly; otherwise a malformed/BER sequence is silently parsed as empty before the caller's size check fires.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.texto: WHAT: BlockedEmail.should_block? reads a record, increments match_count in memory, and calls save, creating a read-modify-write race. WHY: Under concurrent signups with the same blocked email, two processes read the same match_count, both increment to the same value, and both save, losing one update and under-counting blocks. HOW: Use an atomic SQL increment such as BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", Time.zone.now) instead of loading, mutating, and saving the record.

WHAT: emailValidation checks rejectedEmails before trusting authOptions.email_valid, so an OAuth-validated email that was previously rejected manually remains marked invalid. WHY: A user who tries an email via the form, sees it rejected, then authenticates with the same email through OAuth is prevented from submitting even though the provider has validated the address. HOW: Move the authOptions.email/email_valid check above the rejectedEmails check so OAuth-verified emails bypass the client-side rejection cache.

WHAT: validate_each passes the raw value to email_in_restriction_setting? which performs value =~ regexp without guarding against nil. WHY: Updating an existing user with email set to nil causes email_changed? to be true; Rails still runs the email validator after the presence validator fails, and nil =~ regexp raises NoMethodError instead of returning validation errors. HOW: Add an early return if value.blank? at the start of validate_each so blank/nil emails are handled by the presence validator alone.

WHAT: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the email with a case-sensitive exact match (BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first). WHY: On a case-sensitive database (e.g., PostgreSQL default), a blocked address like bad@spam.com can be bypassed by signing up with BAD@SPAM.COM, defeating the email block list. HOW: Use a case-insensitive lookup such as BlockedEmail.where('LOWER(email) = LOWER(?)', email).first, or normalize stored and compared values consistently.

WHAT: EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and updates last_match_at, but the signup controller invokes user.valid? followed by user.save, and each reruns validations. WHY: A single blocked signup attempt increments BlockedEmail.match_count twice, inflating the block statistics. HOW: Move the stats update out of the validator and into the controller path where the signup is actually rejected, or make the increment idempotent per request.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.texto: Global canManage() grants group management to holders of only the VIEW scope on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() gates top-level group creation on requireManage(), so a principal with only view permission can create groups. Change the fallback to require only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, matching UserPermissionsV2 and ClientPermissionsV2.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses Resource.getId() (the generated resource identifier) where it needs Resource.getName() (the group id stored as the resource name). It also passes that generated id into hasPermission(), which calls resourceStore.findByName() and therefore fails to locate the per-group resource. The returned set contains resource UUIDs instead of group IDs, so UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass invalid values into the UserModel.GROUPS query attribute and group-based user search/count returns wrong results. Use groupResource.getName() for both the permission check and the collected result.

Global canManage() treats the VIEW scope as sufficient for management. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls auth.groups().requireManage(), which delegates here, so a principal with only an all-groups VIEW permission can create top-level groups. The fallback permission check should require only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, not VIEW.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses groupResource.getId() as the group identifier. Group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() are named with the group id, while Resource.getId() is the internal resource UUID. The returned set therefore contains resource UUIDs instead of group ids, causing UserModel.GROUPS filtering to match no users and causing the per-resource permission check in hasPermission to fall back to the all-groups resource. Use groupResource.getName() to obtain the group id.

advanced-date-override-handling-and-time.texto: WHAT: Returning true immediately when dateOverrideExist is true skips the busy-time overlap check below. WHY: A host who has a booking inside a date-override window will still be shown as available, because existing busy slots are never evaluated for override-matched slots. HOW: Remove the early return and fall through to the busy.every(...) check so override windows only make slots available when the host is not busy.

WHAT: Both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, so they are identical. WHY: The working-hours check only validates the slot start time and ignores the slot end time, allowing slots that extend past the host's working hours to be marked available. HOW: Compute `end` from `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()` so the entire slot is verified against `workingHour.startTime` and `workingHour.endTime`.

WHAT: The condition compares two Dayjs objects with `===`, which is reference equality and is always false. WHY: A full-day date override (start equal to end) will never be detected, so the intended all-day block/availability behavior is silently ignored. HOW: Replace the `===` comparison with `.isSame()`, e.g. `dayjs(...start).isSame(dayjs(...end))`.

WHAT: The slot-start vs override-end boundary uses `.isAfter()`, which is strict. WHY: A slot that starts exactly when the override ends is actually outside the override window, but it is treated as inside and returned as available. HOW: Use `.isSameOrAfter(...)` so slots starting at the override end time are correctly rejected.

Returning true immediately when dateOverrideExist is true bypasses the busy-time overlap check below. A host who has a date override for the day but already has a conflicting booking will still show as available.

Both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, so they are identical. The working-hours boundary check therefore always compares the slot start minute against the working-hour end time, allowing slots that extend past the host's working day.

The condition compares two Dayjs objects with `===`, which is reference equality and is always false. A full-day unavailable override where start equals end will never be detected, so the slot will be incorrectly kept available.

The slot-start vs override-end boundary uses `.isAfter()`, which is strict. A slot that starts exactly when the override ends is treated as unavailable, whereas it should be allowed (consistent with the start boundary using isBefore/isSame).

advanced-query-processing-architecture-g.texto: Double interpolation of shard-split targets: runShardSplitQuery interpolates queries here and then passes them to runSplitQuery, which now interpolates again (querySplitting.ts:296-299). This applies ad hoc filters a second time and can duplicate label filters after parsers, producing incorrect LogQL. Either skip interpolation in runSplitQuery when invoked from the shard path or pass a flag to avoid re-applying template variables.

advanced-sql-analytics-framework-grafana.texto: enableSqlExpressions() checks FlagSqlExpressions and then ignores the result, always returning false. This is a suspicious shape, but given the PR title explicitly states 'Disable SQL Expressions to prevent RCE and LFI vulnerability,' it appears to be intentional hard-disable logic rather than a bug; it does not alter runtime behavior away from the stated intent.

WHAT: `enableSqlExpressions` always returns false regardless of `FlagSqlExpressions` because it inverts the flag and returns false in both branches. WHY: This makes the feature toggle dead code and contradicts the function name; if the intent is to gate SQL expressions, the feature is permanently disabled, and if the intent is a hard disable, the misleading flag check should be removed. HOW: Either remove the flag check and simply `return false`, or return `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` to honor the toggle.

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.texto: The recurring-event branch uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` to push calendar deletion promises into `apiDeletes` after awaiting `getCalendar`. Because `forEach` does not await async callbacks, those pushes happen after the synchronous `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 has already observed an empty array, so recurring calendar events are not deleted and the cancellation proceeds prematurely. Replace with `Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(async (credential) => ...))` and push/await the resulting promises before line 652.

The reschedule cancellation loop uses `.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` to call `calendar?.deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting`, but the returned promises are discarded. The subsequent `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and router return run before the deletions complete, and any rejection is unhandled. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))`.

The `try/catch` wraps `.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })`, but `forEach` returns immediately and the async callback rejections are not caught by that block. Calendar/video deletion promises are also not awaited before sending the reschedule email. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` inside the try.

Same fire-and-forget pattern as the vital reschedule file: `.forEach(async ...)` inside `try/catch` neither awaits the deletions nor catches async callback errors, so the email is sent before cancellations finish and failures are silently dropped. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))`.

authzservice-improve-authz-caching-grafa.texto: Stale denial cache entries are never cleared after a permission grant. When Check falls through from cached permissions to a fresh DB query and the result is allowed=true, the code only skips the Set but does not delete an existing permDenialCache entry, so subsequent requests keep returning false until the 30s TTL expires even though the user now has access.

The denial cache key joins name and parent with unescaped '_' separators, so different (name, parent) pairs can collide (e.g., name='a' + parent='b_c' vs name='a_b' + parent='c'), causing one resource's denial to be incorrectly applied to another.

List now uses cached permissions without the requery fallback that Check has. If a user's cached action scopes are stale and omit a newly granted dashboard or folder, List silently returns stale results instead of refreshing permissions, so newly authorized resources are hidden for up to the cache TTL.

Check can invoke GetUserIdentifiers twice on the same request: once inside getCachedIdentityPermissions and again inside the fall-through getIdentityPermissions when the cached lookup errors or misses. On a failing user-identifier lookup this repeats the same failing DB query instead of returning the error immediately.

The userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with unescaped '_' separators, so different (name, parent) pairs can collide (e.g., name='a_b'/parent='c' and name='a'/parent='b_c' both produce the same key). This causes the permDenialCache to return the wrong denial entry and make incorrect authorization decisions. Escape or hash the name and parent components, or use a delimiter that cannot appear in valid UIDs.

comprehensive-workflow-reminder-manageme.texto: Rescheduling calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, which cancels the SendGrid send but does not delete the WorkflowReminder row or mark it `cancelled`. The original booking is only updated to CANCELLED, so cascade delete does not remove the row, leaving orphaned email reminder rows (SMS reminders in the same loop are deleted). Delete the row after successful cancellation, or use the non-immediate path so the cron cleans it up.

Async cancellation helpers are invoked inside `Array.forEach` without awaiting. The email helper persists `cancelled: true`, which the cron relies on to cancel the SendGrid send. If the handler returns before the Prisma update completes (e.g., serverless freeze), the cron will not cancel the email and the cancelled booking can still receive the reminder. Replace `forEach` with `Promise.all`/`for...of await` and include the promises in the final `Promise.all`.

Async cancellation helpers are invoked inside `Array.forEach` without awaiting, so the immediate SendGrid cancel request may not complete before the handler returns. The surrounding `try/catch` also cannot catch errors from async `forEach` callbacks. If the cancellation is lost, the previous rescheduled booking still receives its scheduled email. Replace `forEach` with `Promise.all`/`for...of await` and await the cancellations.

WHAT: The async cancellation helpers deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside Array.forEach without awaiting, and their Promises are not collected into the Promise.all at line 497. WHY: The handler can return before the Prisma update that sets cancelled=true (or the SMS delete) is persisted; in a serverless environment the pending work may never complete, so the cron job does not see the reminders as cancelled and still sends the workflow emails for cancelled bookings. HOW: Collect the returned Promises (e.g. with Promise.all(updatedBookings.flatMap(...))) and await them before the final Promise.all/prisma cleanup.

WHAT: During rescheduling, deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are fired inside Array.forEach without awaiting, and the wrapping try/catch cannot catch errors from those asynchronous calls. WHY: The immediate SendGrid cancel and Twilio cancel may not complete before the API response is sent; if the environment is frozen the old booking’s workflow emails are still sent. The try/catch also fails to log failures because forEach does not return the async errors. HOW: Replace forEach with a loop or Promise.all over the reminders and await the cancellation results inside the existing try/catch.

WHAT: The immediateDelete branch in deleteScheduledEmailReminder posts the SendGrid cancel request and returns without updating or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. WHY: Callers that pass immediateDelete=true (e.g. handleNewBooking rescheduling) leave stale scheduled reminders in the database with scheduled=true and cancelled unset; those rows are never matched by the cron cancellation query and persist until their scheduledDate passes, causing incorrect data and confusing future cancellation attempts. HOW: After a successful SendGrid cancel in the immediateDelete branch, delete the WorkflowReminder row (consistent with deleteScheduledSMSReminder) or set cancelled=true so the cron can clean it up.

database-performance-optimizations-grafa.texto: The background cleanup ticker was reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute. clean() runs with a 9-minute timeout and has no mutex or server-lock guard, so multiple cleanup passes will overlap and all cleanup jobs (annotations, snapshots, temp files, etc.) will execute far more frequently than intended. Restore the 10-minute interval unless a 1-minute cadence was deliberately designed and serialized.

The cleanup code logs normal batch progress at Error level and always includes an 'err' key even when err is nil. This produces false-error log lines that can trigger alerting and obscure real failures. Switch these messages to Debug/Info level and omit the err key when there is no error.

Each cleanup batch logs the full ids slice at Error level. With AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize as large as 32767, every log line can contain tens of thousands of integer IDs, causing excessive log volume and memory/IO overhead. Log only the count, not the entire slice.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.texto: OptimizedCursorPaginator is hard-coded for integer keys but is used with a DateTimeField. get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the raw datetime value, which raises TypeError, and value_from_cursor returns the numeric cursor value instead of a datetime so build_queryset compares the datetime column to the wrong type. Use datetime-aware key conversion (like DateTimePaginator) when ordering by datetime, or use DateTimePaginator as the base for this endpoint.

The negative-offset branch passes a negative start index to queryset slicing (e.g., queryset[cursor.offset:...]). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start indices and raises an exception, so a caller-supplied cursor with a negative offset will 500 instead of enabling efficient reverse pagination. Either reject/ignore negative offsets or implement reverse pagination by flipping the ordering and cursor value, not by negative slicing.

OptimizedCursorPaginator assumes numeric order_by keys but OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses it with order_by='-datetime'. get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on a datetime, which raises TypeError when build_cursor generates next/prev cursors; value_from_cursor returns a raw numeric cursor value that is then compared against a datetime column in build_queryset. Either make this paginator datetime-aware (like DateTimePaginator) or do not use it for datetime-ordered audit logs.

The 'advanced' negative-offset branch passes a negative start index to Django QuerySet slicing (queryset[cursor.offset:...]), which raises AssertionError because Django does not support negative indexing on QuerySets. Remove or replace this branch with a valid bounded implementation; the current code will crash for any admin/superuser who supplies a negative cursor offset.

organization_context.member.has_global_access is dereferenced without a None check, but RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is documented as nullable when the user has no membership in the organization. For non-superusers where member is None this raises AttributeError. Guard the access with getattr(organization_context.member, 'has_global_access', False) or a None check.

feat-add-calendar-cache-status-and-actio.texto: The authorization check only matches `userId: user.id`, so team-owned credentials (where `userId` is null and ownership is `teamId`) fail the lookup and return "Credential not found or access denied". Existing `deleteCredentialHandler` accepts a `teamId` and routes the query through `teamId` or `userId`; this handler should do the same so team members and admins can delete cache for team calendars.

The handler directly constructs `CalendarCacheRepository` instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()`/`initFromCredentialId()`, which checks the `calendar-cache` feature flag and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when disabled. When the feature is off globally, this still executes a `CalendarCache` `groupBy` query on every connectedCalendars call for no benefit and can expose stale cache status. Use the existing `CalendarCache.init*` factory or gate the query with the feature flag.

The `deleteCacheMutation` only invokes the parent `onSuccess` callback and does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. If the parent `onChanged` does not refetch, the dropdown continues to display the old `cacheUpdatedAt` after a successful deletion. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess`, matching the behavior of `disconnectMutation`.

The script uses `sed -i '' -E`, which is macOS-specific and errors on Linux because GNU sed interprets the empty string after `-i` as the backup-file argument. Use a portable form such as `sed -i.bak -E ...` and remove the backup, or branch on `uname` to keep the script runnable on both platforms.

feat-upsampling-support-upsampled-error-.texto: _get_event_stats passes the captured outer `dataset` to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects instead of the `scoped_dataset` parameter. In the dashboard-widget split path _get_event_stats is called with `discover` for errors-only queries (organization_events_stats.py:365), but the helper evaluates the original metrics dataset and returns False, so error upsampling is skipped even when every project is allowlisted. Pass `scoped_dataset` to the helper.

_is_error_focused_query reads the query from `request.GET` instead of the actual `query` string being executed. The dashboard-widget split path rewrites the executed query to errors-only or transactions-only (organization_events_stats.py:362, 405), so the helper evaluates the user's original query and can make the wrong upsampling decision for the query that actually runs. Change the helper to accept the query string and pass the actual `query` from _get_event_stats.

_is_error_focused_query uses a naive substring check (`"event.type:error" in query`), so a negated query like `!event.type:error` matches and incorrectly enables upsampling for a non-error query. Parse the query or at least reject matches preceded by `!`.

_are_all_projects_error_upsampled tests membership with `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)`, which is O(N×M) and is invoked on every events-stats call (multiple times in the widget-split path). Convert `allowlist` to a set before the all() check to make it O(N).

WHAT: `_get_event_stats` decides whether to upsample using the outer request `dataset` instead of the `scoped_dataset` that will actually execute the query. WHY: In the `metrics_enhanced` dashboard-widget split path, `scoped_dataset` is switched to `discover` but the captured `dataset` is still a metrics module, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns `False` and allowlisted error queries are not upsampled even though they run against `discover`. HOW: pass `scoped_dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` instead of `dataset`.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.texto: WHAT: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join() ignores its timeout argument and calls self.close() instead of waiting for in-flight work. WHY: Arroyo expects join(timeout) to block up to the given timeout while work drains; delegating to close() with fixed 5s timeouts can abort work early or exceed the caller's deadline. HOW: Implement join() to wait on the queue pool and commit thread using the supplied timeout, only signaling shutdown if not already closed.

WHAT: FilteredPayload messages do not have their offsets tracked or committed. WHY: submit() calls decode_payload first, which raises AssertionError for FilteredPayload, and the exception handler only records offsets when message.value is a BrokerValue; FilteredPayload messages are skipped, so the consumer will reprocess from that offset. HOW: Check message.value type before decoding and immediately add/complete the offset for FilteredPayload messages without invoking the decoder.

WHAT: get_committable_offsets() holds the partition lock while scanning every offset in the uncommitted window. WHY: A large backlog or one slow item creates a wide offset range, making this O(window size) and blocking all other threads touching that partition. HOW: Track the lowest outstanding offset per partition (e.g., with a sorted structure or heap) so the committable offset can be found in O(log N) or O(1) without a linear scan.

close() shuts down the commit thread before waiting for workers to finish. Offsets completed after the commit loop's final pass are never committed, so messages will be reprocessed on consumer restart. Restructure close() to drain the queue pool first, then signal the commit thread for a final commit, then join it.

queue.Queue() is unbounded and submit() never checks depth, so there is no backpressure when producers outpace workers. A traffic burst can exhaust memory. Set a maxsize on the queues and let put() block, or add an explicit depth limit / backpressure check before enqueueing.

feature-per-topic-unsubscribe-option-in-.texto: TopicsController#unsubscribe assumes a TopicUser row always exists. When TopicUser.find_by returns nil, calling tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the request crashes before any unsubscribe happens. Use TopicUser.change (which creates the row if missing) or guard against nil before mutating.

The action directly assigns and saves notification_level, bypassing TopicUser.change. This leaves notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id stale and skips the MessageBus notification_level_change broadcast that every other notification-level update performs, breaking the established invariant for manual level changes.

The unsubscribe action is registered as a GET route that mutates the user's notification level. Rails CSRF protection only verifies non-GET requests, so a malicious site can embed or tags pointing to /t/.../unsubscribe and force an authenticated user to unsubscribe. Require a signed per-user token for email links or change the web flow to POST with CSRF verification.

The per-topic unsubscribe_url passed to Email::MessageBuilder is a relative path because Topic#unsubscribe_url returns "#{url}/unsubscribe" and Topic#url is relative. Email clients cannot resolve relative URLs in message bodies, so the unsubscribe link in sent emails will be broken. Pass an absolute URL by prepending Discourse.base_url, consistent with how user_preferences_url is built.

TopicsController#unsubscribe creates @topic_view before mutating and saving the TopicUser notification_level. perform_show_response then preloads that stale TopicView into the Ember bootstrap store as topic_#{id}. The client route's PostStream.loadTopicView reads PreloadStore before making an AJAX request, so the unsubscribe page renders the old notification level. Recreate or reload @topic_view after the save before calling perform_show_response.

implement-recovery-key-support-for-user-.texto: Recovery authentication codes are stored as a JSON list of raw, unhashed values in the user storage credentialData field. This exposes the codes in plaintext if the in-memory store is inspected or if this provider is used as a reference implementation. Hash the codes with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode before storage and compare hashed values during validation, matching RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.

isValid returns true when any stored raw recovery code matches the raw input but never removes or marks the used code as consumed. Unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider, which consumes each code on use, this allows a captured or leaked recovery code to be reused indefinitely, breaking single-use semantics. Remove or invalidate the matched code after a successful validation.

getCredentials reconstructs a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the stored raw codes but does not preserve the stored credential ID. The returned model therefore has a null ID, so operations that rely on the credential ID such as removeStoredCredentialById will fail or target the wrong credential. Copy myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() onto the reconstructed model.

The authenticator now retrieves a credential that can be stored in an external user storage provider, but then calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...) when all codes are used. removeStoredCredentialById only operates on Keycloak's local/federated credential store (UserCredentialManager.getStoreForUser returns userLocalStorage or userFederatedStorage), not on credentials held by the external UserStorageProvider. When all recovery codes are consumed, the external credential is therefore never removed, leaving a stale credential that may still be accepted by the provider.

hasRecoveryCodes looks up userPasswords.get(username) without calling translateUserName(username), while every other access in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage uses translateUserName, which lowercases the username. For any non-lowercase username the lookup misses and the method incorrectly returns false, making the assertion inconsistent with the actual storage state.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.texto: WHAT: `max_segment_spans` is still accepted and stored in `SpansBuffer.__init__` but the span-count guard was removed from `load_segments`, so the limit is now silently ignored. WHY: Callers passing a custom `max_segment_spans` expect it to bound segment size, but the only enforcement is the hardcoded `1000` inside `add-buffer.lua`, breaking the class contract. HOW: Either wire `max_segment_spans` through to the Lua script as the eviction threshold and restore the flush-time guard, or remove the parameter from the public constructor.

WHAT: `zpopmin` evicts spans purely by the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` score, with no hierarchy-aware protection for root or ancestor spans. WHY: If a root/ancestor span ends earlier than its descendants (clock skew, async children, etc.) it will be removed even though the PR states hierarchy is prioritized; the separate `has_root_span` flag stays set, so the segment can later be flushed as if it contains a root span when the root payload is actually gone. HOW: Boost the scores of segment/root spans or exclude them from eviction so ancestors are never dropped before their descendants.

WHAT: `redis.call("zunionstore", ...)` is invoked without an `AGGREGATE` modifier, so Redis sums the scores of any member present in both source sets. WHY: Duplicate span payloads (e.g., from Kafka at-least-once redelivery or spans reachable through multiple redirect merges) get an `end_timestamp_precise` score that is a sum of timestamps rather than the true timestamp, which corrupts eviction order so duplicates are unfairly retained and genuinely old spans may be evicted first. HOW: Add `"AGGREGATE", "MAX"` to both `zunionstore` calls so duplicate members keep the true/latest end timestamp.

WHAT: `zpopmin` evicts spans based solely on the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` score, with no consideration for hierarchy depth. WHY: A root or parent span with an older end timestamp than its children can be evicted before them, leaving descendant spans without their segment root/parent and producing incomplete or orphaned segments when flushed. HOW: Encode hierarchy depth into the sorted-set score (e.g., higher depth-weight for ancestors) or store root/segment spans in a protected key so they are never evicted.

WHAT: The `max_segment_spans` span-count guard was removed from `flush_segments`, while `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts and stores the parameter and `add-buffer.lua` hardcodes a limit of 1000. WHY: Callers and configuration that set a non-default `max_segment_spans` are silently ignored, creating a contract mismatch between the configured limit and the actual enforced limit. HOW: Either remove the now-obsolete `max_segment_spans` parameter from `SpansBuffer` and its callers, or pass the configured value into the Lua script and use it in place of the hardcoded 1000.

scale-color-lightness-must-use-secondary.texto: The light-theme argument of `dark-light-choose` uses lightness 70% instead of the original 30%. This changes `.topic-meta-data h5 a` in light themes from a slightly lightened primary to a much lighter gray, contradicting the PR's stated intent to only fix dark themes. Change to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

The light-theme argument of `dark-light-choose` uses lightness 30% instead of the original 70%. This makes `.custom-message-length` much darker in light themes than before and inconsistent with the desktop modal style (desktop/modal.scss:94). Change to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

The light-theme argument of `dark-light-choose` uses lightness 50% instead of the original 20%. This changes `.topic-map h3` in light themes from a dark gray to a medium gray and is inconsistent with the desktop equivalent (desktop/topic-post.scss:321).
